units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
You shall see. All religious organizations exist by selling themselves to the rich.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Not the Army. That is the Church of the poor.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: All the more reason for buying it.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: I don't think you quite know what the Army does for the poor.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Oh yes I do. It draws their teeth: that is enough for me--as a man of business--
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Nonsense! It makes them sober--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: I prefer sober workmen. The profits are larger.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: --honest--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Honest workmen are the most economical.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: --attached to their homes--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: So much the better: they will put up with anything sooner than change their shop.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: --happy--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: An invaluable safeguard against revolution.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: --unselfish--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Indifferent to their own interests, which suits me exactly.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: --with their thoughts on heavenly things--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [rising] And not on Trade Unionism nor Socialism.
Excellent.
CUSINS [revolted] You really are an infernal old rascal.
UNDERSHAFT [indicating Peter Shirley, who has just came from the shelter and strolled dejectedly down the yard between them] And this is an honest man!
Yes; and what av I got by it?
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: he passes on bitterly and sits on the form, in the corner of the penthouse.
Snobby Price, beaming sanctimoniously, and Jenny Hill, with a tambourine full of coppers, come from the shelter and go to the drum, on which Jenny begins to count the money.
UNDERSHAFT [replying to Shirley] Oh, your employers must have got a good deal by it from first to last. [He sits on the table, with one foot on the side form.
Cusins, overwhelmed, sits down on the same form nearer the shelter.
Barbara comes from the shelter to the middle of the yard.
She is excited and a little overwrought].
We've just had a splendid experience meeting at the other gate in Cripps's lane. I've hardly ever seen them so much moved as they were by your confession, Mr Price.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: I could almost be glad of my past wickedness if I could believe that it would elp to keep hathers stright.
units.name: PRICE

units.text: So it will, Snobby. How much, Jenny?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Four and tenpence, Major.
units.name: JENNY

units.text: Oh Snobby, if you had given your poor mother just one more kick, we should have got the whole five shillings!
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: If she heard you say that, miss, she'd be sorry I didn't. But I'm glad. Oh what a joy it will be to her when she hears I'm saved!
units.name: PRICE

units.text: Shall I contribute the odd twopence, Barbara? The millionaire's mite, eh?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: He takes a couple of pennies from his pocket.
How did you make that twopence?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: As usual. By selling cannons, torpedoes, submarines, and my new patent Grand Duke hand grenade.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Put it back in your pocket. You can't buy your Salvation here for twopence: you must work it out.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Is twopence not enough? I can afford a little more, if you press me.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Two million millions would not be enough. There is bad blood on your hands; and nothing but good blood can cleanse them. Money is no use. Take it away.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She turns to Cusins.
Dolly: you must write another letter for me to the papers.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: He makes a wry face.

Yes: I know you don't like it; but it must be done. The starvation this winter is beating us: everybody is unemployed. The General says we must close this shelter if we cant get more money. I force the collections at the meetings until I am ashamed, don't I, Snobby?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: It's a fair treat to see you work it, miss. The way you got them up from three-and-six to four-and-ten with that hymn, penny by penny and verse by verse, was a caution. Not a Cheap Jack on Mile End Waste could touch you at it.
units.name: PRICE

units.text: Yes; but I wish we could do without it. I am getting at last to think more of the collection than of the people's souls. And what are those hatfuls of pence and halfpence? We want thousands! tens of thousands! hundreds of thousands! I want to convert people, not to be always begging for the Army in a way I'd die sooner than beg for myself.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [in profound irony] Genuine unselfishness is capable of anything, my dear.
BARBARA [unsuspectingly, as she turns away to take the money from the drum and put it in a cash bag she carries] Yes, isn't it? [Undershaft looks sardonically at Cusins].
CUSINS [aside to Undershaft] Mephistopheles!
Machiavelli!
